<issue>
Subtitle Edit 5.1.0 beta 8 (Linux)
After deleting all previous configuration files and letting Subtitle Edit recreate them, the application behavior changed in several areas, so the configuration was successfully reset.

However, OCR corrections from spa_OCRFixReplaceList.xml are still not applied.

Test subtitle:

Hola, aca estoy.
Adios.
Algun dia volvere.

Run:
Tools -> Fix common errors

Enable only:
Fix common OCR errors using OCR replace list

Expected:

Hola, acá estoy.
Adiós.
Algún día volveré.

Actual:

No corrections are made.

The same subtitle and the same
spa_OCRFixReplaceList.xml file work correctly in Subtitle Edit 4.0.16 (Mono).

MD5 of spa_OCRFixReplaceList.xml:
cf66622261fa292b75b79799acb202b1

The OCR replacement file exists and is identical in both installations.

</issue>

The repository is at /testbed.

input.instruction: In /testbed (Subtitle Edit C#), find the "Fix common errors" rule for "Fix common OCR errors using OCR replace list" (likely FixOcrErrorsViaReplaceList in src/**/Logic/CommonErrors or similar) and the OCR fix replace list loading code (OcrFixReplaceList, LoadReplaceList, spa_OCRFixReplaceList.xml). Report the full source of the rule and of OcrFixReplaceList's relevant methods (file paths+line numbers), especially how words are matched and which language/culture is used to load the file.

content.content: {"summary":"The FixCommonOcrErrors rule is a thin wrapper. All matching happens in OcrFixReplaceList2, which OcrFixEngine loads by three-letter ISO language code (for example 'spa'), not by culture. Nothing here uses CultureInfo. I read the sources but did not run or modify anything.","findings":["Rule: src/ui/Features/Tools/FixCommonErrors/FixCommonOcrErrors.cs:11-62. It returns early if the static OcrFixEngine is null. It converts callbacks.Language (two-letter code) to a three-letter code with Iso639Dash2LanguageCode.GetThreeLetterCodeFromTwoLetterCode (line 28) and returns if that is empty. It then looks for a spell-check dictionary whose GetThreeLetterCode() matches (lines 34-40) and returns if none is found. It calls OcrFixEngine.Initialize(subtitle, threeLetterCode, spellChecker) at line 42. For each paragraph it calls OcrFixEngine.FixOcrErrors(i, p.Text, true) (line 49), and when the text changes it logs it via callbacks.AddFixToListView and sets p.Text. There is no class named FixOcrErrorsViaReplaceList.","Loader class: src/libuilogic/Ocr/FixEngine/OcrFixReplaceList2.cs. There is no class named OcrFixReplaceList or method named LoadReplaceList(file); the class is OcrFixReplaceList2.","Language and file choice: OcrFixReplaceList2.cs:203-206, FromLanguageId(languageId) opens Path.Combine(SpellCheckConfig.DictionariesFolder(), languageId + \"_OCRFixReplaceList.xml\"). The postfix constant is at line 35. For Spanish the file is spa_OCRFixReplaceList.xml in the dictionaries folder.","OcrFixEngine.cs:55-70, IOcrFixEngine.Initialize, derives the two-letter code from the three-letter code for the spell checker. It then calls OcrFixReplaceList2.FromLanguageId(_threeLetterIsoLanguageName) at line 69. A default empty list is created at line 49.","Constructor, lines 39-200: it loads the main XML via LoadXmlReplaceListDocument (lines 1109-1130) and a user file via LoadXmlReplaceListUserDocument (lines 1134-1155). The user file is _User.xml (line 1132). A missing or invalid file gives an empty default document, and the error goes into ErrorMessage.","LoadReplaceList(XmlDocument doc, string name) is at lines 208-236. It reads the child nodes of the named section and builds a Dictionary from each node's from/to attributes. Duplicate keys are ignored and invalid nodes are skipped. The sections are WholeWords, PartialWordsAlways, PartialWords, PartialLines, PartialLinesAlways, BeginLines, EndLines and WholeLines. LoadRegExList (line 238) handles RegularExpressions. SpellCheckRegex.LoadRegExList handles RegularExpressionsIfSpelledCorrectly. The user file's Removed* sections then delete entries, and its additions are added if the key is not already present.","Word matching, FixCommonWordErrors (593-727), is called from OcrFixEngine.cs:265 per word. The dictionary lookups use default Dictionary comparison, which is case-sensitive and ordinal, with no culture. It first applies hardcoded rules if Configuration.Settings.Tools.OcrFixUseHardcodedRules is set: ligatures, Greek nu to v (skipped when the file name contains '\\ell_OCRFixReplaceList.xml'), and normalising quote characters to '. It then does plain string.Replace for every _partialWordAlwaysReplaceList key. It strips prefixes and suffixes (, newlines, leading -, ., \" and (, and trailing \".,!?)]:; and ) into pre and post, and inserts a space after a '?' followed by a letter (RegExQuestion). It then calls GetReplaceWord (729-769), which tries these exact keys in order: pre+word+post, pre+word, word+post, word. If nothing matches and the hardcoded rules change the word, it retries the lookup. Those rules fix I/1 or 0 inside lowercase words and a lowercase l inside uppercase words.","Line-level matching, FixOcrErrorViaLineReplaceList (309-442), is called from OcrFixEngine.cs:108. It runs these steps in order: WholeLines exact match; BeginLines (StartsWith and after '. ', '! ', '? ' or a quote); EndLines (EndsWith, skipped if SkipAddLineEnding); PartialLines via static ReplaceWord; PartialLinesAlways via plain Replace; regexes in RegularExpressions (Multiline, cached); and, only when !spelledOK, the spell-checked regexes.","ReplaceWord (static, 1266-1318) does ordinal matching on whole-word boundaries. A boundary is punctuation, whitespace or one of the characters in separatorChars at line 1276. A word starting with a space always counts as start-OK, and a replacement ending with a space counts as end-OK.","User additions: AddWordOrPartial (1157-1182) saves entries containing a space to PartialLines and all others to WholeWords in the _User.xml file. RemoveWordOrPartial is at 1001."],"confidence":0.85}

Also check CheckAndFixWord: for a misspelled word like "aca" in Spanish, does it call _ocrFixReplaceList.FixCommonWordErrors and set FixedWord? Print code with line numbers.

content.content: {"summary":"GetText does use FixedWord. CheckAndFixWord calls FixCommonWordErrors for 'aca' (unless _changeAllDictionary has it) and sets FixedWord on every path. I didn't check whether the Spanish replace list actually changes 'aca'.","findings":["OcrFixLineResult is in OcrFixLineResult.cs:5. If the replace list did not change the word, FixedWord equals the original word.","Line 299 calls splitLine.GetText() while the current word's FixedWord is still empty, so GetText falls back to the original Word for that word.","Line 88 sets FixedWord = Word for words that skip checking."],"confidence":0.9}

I read the code only and ran nothing.","findings":["SpellCheckDictionaryDisplay.GetThreeLetterCode (src/libuilogic/SpellCheck/SpellCheckDictionaryDisplay.cs) calls GetTwoLetterLanguageCode. content.text:
I made one change, but I couldn't confirm it fixes your whole test subtitle. I haven't built it or run any tests.

**What I found:** the Spanish list only has lowercase entries, such as `adios` → `adiós` and `algun` → `algún`. The lookup is case-sensitive, so `Adios` and `Algun` at the start of a line never matched. That explains those two lines.

**The fix:** in `src/libuilogic/Ocr/FixEngine/OcrFixReplaceList2.cs`, `GetReplaceWord` now tries the exact word first. If that fails and the word starts with a capital, it retries with a lowercase first letter. It then restores the capital on the result, so `Adios` becomes `Adiós`.

**What's still open:** `Hola, aca estoy.` contains only a lowercase `aca`, which was already in the list. It should have been corrected before my change, so the capitalisation bug doesn't explain your report that nothing changed. I read the code path and found no bug for Spanish. I did find silent early returns in the rule that could explain "no corrections at all":
- **Dictionary file type:** only `.dic` files in the dictionaries folder are listed, so if Spanish is installed only as an `.hunspell` file, the rule does nothing.
- **Missing folder:** if the dictionaries folder doesn't exist, the rule does nothing.
- **Detected language:** the rule uses the language detected from your subtitle, so a wrong detection (not `es`) skips the Spanish list.

On the Linux install, check that `es_ES.dic` is in the dictionaries folder next to `spa_OCRFixReplaceList.xml`. Also check that the subtitle is detected as Spanish.
